# Blip Golf

> Blip is a golf ball finder: a marker pen (Blip Pen) plus a MagSafe clip-on camera for iPhone (Blip Cam). You mark the ball you already play before the round; when you lose it, Blip Cam fires a flash your eyes can't see, waits a split second, then looks, so grass and sunlight stay dark and your mark shows up as a dot on the phone screen. Walk to the dot. Prototype stage, built in the open by a solo golfer-founder.

## Status (honest)
- Working: the infrared prototype camera spots a ball in the open.
- Working: flash and capture are synced to the millionth of a second.
- Testing: Blip Pen long-glow mineral pigment ink.
- Testing: a marked ball under leaves in full daylight. Blip is designed for daylight; this is not proven yet.

## Pricing and launch
- Launching on Kickstarter (pre-launch page not live yet).
- Early bird: $79 USD, first 200 units. Retail: $149 USD.
- Built for iPhone with MagSafe.
- For casual rounds only: under Rule 4.3a of the Rules of Golf, devices like this aren't allowed in competition rounds.

## How it compares
- Searching by eye: free, but a covered ball is invisible.
- Blue-tint glasses and filter apps: only help when the ball is already visible.
- UV flashlights: only work at night.
- RF tracking balls: need special balls (about £26 each) and only work at close range.
- Blip: works with your own ball and your own iPhone; daylight and under-leaves performance is designed for and being tested now.

## FAQ
- Does Blip work with my own golf balls? Yes, any ball marked with the Blip Pen. No special balls, no battery or tag in the ball.
- Does it work in daylight? It is designed for daylight and being tested now. Results will be posted either way.
- Is it legal in tournaments? No. Casual rounds only (Rule 4.3a).
